utterances.text: If I tell you that this map shows the front lines in green or slightly more blue are the positions of the BH army, and the dark green indicates the positions of your army, if I may put it that way, that is, the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska, would you agree with me that as they are drawn here, do they reflect the true positions in September 1992 to August 1994?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It's a leading question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness is asked after he has first given the front lines whether this line would reflect or not -- I think the witness could answer that question. But could we first perhaps see -- I have some difficulties in seeing dark and -- could we zoom out a tiny little bit. Could we zoom out or is that impossible? That's as wide as it can be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I think you said something about green lines and more bluish green lines. I'm trying to spot them on this map. I only see one colour of green, if I'm -- but it might be that I'm slightly blind for colours. But could you perhaps tell me where to find the more dark green lines.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: The dark green lines -- or rather, dark green are in relation to the circle and the word "Brijesce," below the large red circle and above the word "Brijesce."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then the lighter green lines -- oh, now I see them, I think. Could we just perhaps first have a look at the colour map. Could Mr. Usher bring them so that we first have a look at it, and then we can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. It's entirely clear now. It's my bad side that caused -- well, also, of course, but the bad side on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krsman, I told you that the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska and of the Army of BH are indicated here. Can you tell us, the dark -- the darker green lines - and I told you that those were the positions of the BH army - do they reflect the positions of the army between September 1992 to August 1994?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: The BH army's positions are correct, and they reflect the situation. But the positions of our army, of Republika Srpska, I've already drawn it and I indicated them. These as shown here do not reflect the true situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Will you take the black marker to identify the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska, please.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: I've already said, because we could not defend this -- like this. And here we went -- because this is blown up. We broke off that line and we followed the tracks, apart from the big buildings. And I drew it on the previous map, because they were destroyed straight away so we could not use them. So this is what our line was, and it never changed during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark on this map the area of the depot and the Bozica pump or petrol station.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: The area of depot, you can see. You can see all these tracks, and that is all part of it. And the Bozica pump was on the high street and on the main road, and it's still there, except that it's not called the Bozica pump but something else. I don't know what.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Between 1992 to -- that is, September -- August 1994, did you with your company -- were you with your company in the area which you marked as the area of the 1st Company in the sense of your military engagement?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes. On one occasion, and that was on Sveti Sava, which is the 27th of January, 1993. The enemy forces had broken through the lines in the area of Spajic farm, killed a soldier. Other soldiers beat a retreat. And then with some men I managed to regain this line and to reinstitute the previous state of affairs. But whenever it was necessary in case of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. more fierce attacks, we went there, and they also came to help us, but they were all our friends, our kums, our relatives.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You've marked the position of the depot of the railway station and the Bozica pump, but you said the Bozica pump was in the territory which is near the road. That is, it is between the positions of the Army of BH and the Army of Republika Srpska. Did you have any information if in the territory of the Bozica pump there were any troops at that time?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes, there were troops. And people who had come out of the city told me -- of course, every pump has fuel. Since there was a shortage in the city, they risked, and they were getting the fuel from tankers, from systems at the pump. So that is a detail that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On this map we see a point marked "16" and "17." Can you tell us, since you looked at the map of the city, and that street can -- is also drawn on that map -- can you tell us how far is it from the railway station, or rather, the depot to this point which is marked with numbers "16" and "17."

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Well, you can only calculate it on the map. This is Brijesko Brdo and from here, from the depot you cannot see this point. Perhaps if you are a bit to the right. But there must be at least a kilometre from the depot to the 16/17 point.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that from the depot you cannot see this point, can you explain why can't you see it?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Well, simply you can't because this road -- all these roads go between hills, and the depot -- I don't know what is the feature. Well, it's 492, and this is 700, and there is absolutely a hill. It's called Brijesko Brdo. You simply can't see that point from the depot. I was born there, and I know it. It's impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm wondering, Ms. Pilipovic -- I understood the position of the Prosecution not to be that it was ever fired from the depot. And we now have -- we get testimony at length as that what you could not see from the depot. But I'm just trying to understand what is actually going on. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, you've correctly stated the Prosecution position with respect to the alleged sniper position. It's clearly indicated on the map and that's not the depot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So there's no way that the Prosecution takes it that 16 and 17 could be seen -- or could be directly targeted from the depot or the railway station.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no position on that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there's no dispute about that, Ms. Pilipovic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. I merely have to say the issue of the depot, in view of the testimonies of witnesses of the Prosecution, I wanted to clear this up because some witnesses at times said that there was fire opened from the area of the depot. So my next question will be, as we can see this red circle here. And that is why I wanted the Bozica pump to be marked, because some witnesses spoke about Bozica pump and the depot, and I wanted to clear this up. As the witness lived in the area -- my question was to be:

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krsman, on this map you can also see a rather large red circle on this map, can't you?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you identify this area?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: I can. This is the area of Bacici. So roughly these are meadows -- these are farms which were tilled by these people, the beginning of these farms, those people who lived over here in Brijesce.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "the area of Bacici," can you tell us this area, the area of Bacici - so it's September 1992/August 1994 - what kind of population and who lived in that area? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Well, naturally, nobody lived in that area, because I've already said that in May we had already retreated to the barracks and to the line that I've shown you. So this was an abandoned territory which was farmed by people -- which had been farmed by people before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if during the war in that area which you tell us was abandoned - and that was land that was farmed beforehand - were there any army troops or were there any positions in that place?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Absolutely not, because it was indefencible. It was in the middle of meadows. Any position would have been destroyed. And very simply -- I mean, had there have been a command down there, I would have destroyed it immediately, had there been any position there of any importance.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said "up." What did you mean by the word "up"?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Well, in the beginning of my testimony, I said that Brijesko Brdo is up there. That is, that all the Muslim positions were up on the hill and we were down. If you know what area I'm talking about, then you know what it means to you. Brijesko Brdo is a huge hill above us, and we were all down in the valley.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel and witness please break between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please wait until the interpreters have been able to translate the question before you answer it. And just for my information, Ms. Pilipovic, the "B" marked on this map as we see it in front of us, what was that exactly again?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that the pump?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the Bozica pump, the petrol station. That is what the witness marked on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krsman, if we assume that army troops could be here, where this circle is, can you tell us, in relation to the point 16 and 17, what -- how feasible is it to -- for the infantry to act against the point 16 and 17?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. Calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said "I assume." I said "let us assume that army troops are there," since the witness told us what kind of terrain we were dealing with here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me first again read your question. Yes. I don't know what kind of feasibility you have in mind. So if the witness knows about the terrain, you can ask him questions about that. But whether it's feasible or not depends on many, many circumstances. Some of them would call for speculation. Others might not call for speculation. So if you would try to ask the witness about facts he knows, that would be the best way. And it could be on this subject. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krsman, do you -- are you familiar with positions in the area of this circle that you can see on the map? Do you know, that is, that area?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes, of course I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us something about the lie of the land between this circle and points 16 and 17? Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: From the circle to this intersection, you can see it on the map, it's flat. You have, for instance, this feature 492 elevation. Towards the intersection there is a steep slope here. I think it's about 700-something, which means that there is about a 200-metre difference in altitude.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Since you've given us this clarification -- since you've given us this explanation, since you've explained to us the difference in altitude, can you tell us something about the distance between the circle and the point 16 and 17? According to you, how far are they?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Well, it can be easily measured, but I'm quite sure that it's over 600 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that you attended the morning briefings almost daily. Does this mean that commanders of the 1st and the 2nd Company also attended those briefings?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes, always, either the commanders or their deputies.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you were present when they reported on their daily, if I may call them that, reports, on the daily developments? Did you hear the reports of the 1st Company commander? For instance, what was the military situation in the area of responsibility of the 1st Company?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: The situation in the area of responsibility of the 1st Company was almost identical with the situation in the area of responsibility of the 2nd and mine, that is, the 3rd Company. That is simply because we were in the valley, so that we daily suffered provocations and fire. For a while we made jokes about that. They could even hit us with a stone. There were daily provocations -- well, perhaps not every day, but every week surely.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: At some point in your testimony you mentioned the cease-fire. Can you tell us if you, that is, have any knowledge about that, whether -- whether you were kept abreast of the cease-fire agreements signed. And if so, often were you aware of those cease-fires and were they complied with, and could you also place them in time?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: There were frequent agreements on the cease-fires, especially after offensives when they could not break through our territory. Then they requested these cease-fires, as opposed to simply consolidate their forces. And we really -- I can say that openly we always strictly complied with the signed cease-fire agreements, always, and nothing but. I am talking about my company, but I also know about the other two companies, that we were never the first ones to violate those cease-fires.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the map of the city - and now we see on this map too - could you indicate the road that was, if I understood you properly -- that was the road that was used throughout the war. We're talking about September 1992/August 1994. Can you point at this road on the map?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: I don't understand. Which road do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I mean the road that you indicated on the map of the city, the road, the communication.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: For -- my company used a village road behind the depot. But the main road, the highway to the city was used by UNPROFOR, by observers, and the others. That is, none of the -- neither of the belligerents used the highway.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can understand from your explanation, the highway, the main road, passed through -- and to try to make it more precise, it went through these points and this circle down there and through points 16 and 17.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes, exactly across this intersection, across this spaghetti junction, because there was -- there was this bifurcation where one went to Ilidza and one followed the Buca Potok and also went on to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in view of the witness's answers, the Defence should like to show a photograph which is Prosecution Exhibit 1812A. I have informed the registrar that I wanted to show the witness this map -- I mean, this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you before to -- just to have clarified. Yes. No, it's clear to me -- it's clear to me now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krsman, you have in front of you a photograph reflecting two areas. Can you tell us whether you recognise the area on the upper photograph.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes. I've just explained it. It's -- on that map it must be the circle. And what you see in the background are the houses of the Bozic family. And our line was right next to those houses. And what we see in front, it's either a shed or a hen house, as we call it. And right in the foreground, we see the meadows that I spoke about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we perhaps further zoom in, and could the photograph be put in such a way that we have -- yes. And could you perhaps -- that would certainly assist, Ms. Pilipovic. Could you ask the witness to point at the map from where this view comes and what he sees and what is in the circle so that we are better able to follow his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krsman, can you tell us, the area which is now shown on the upper photograph in this way, could you tell us from which positions can you see this area?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: You can see this area from one of the streets across the Bozica pump. Now, I see the lower photograph, so I know what this is about -- I mean, I know which street it is. So it's from one of the streets across the road from the Bozica pump.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind that on the map that I showed you you marked the red circle -- that is, you said that between the red circle and points 16 Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and 17 there was a road between them. Do we see on this map this part of the road?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: As you can see, you can't even see the railway line. You can't see the road. You can't see the junction, and you can't see the other road either. You can't see anything from this position, from position X. It's been -- this photograph was taken from position X. None of what one should be able to see down below can be seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you're telling us that this area was photographed from position X.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we have a position X yet, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I think it can be seen in the other photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is this what you were thinking of?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I can see both photographs. I didn't realise that the Chamber couldn't see them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, where would that be on the map? Because that's what interests me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll now ask the witness to mark that on the map, to mark the position from which this area was photographed, the area that we can see in the upper photograph.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: It's more or less where this circle is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we looking in the direction of where the circle is, or is the photograph taken from the point where the circle is?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krsman, could you explain this to us.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: The first photograph was taken - and I'm referring to this first one that has the circle here - it was photographed from this position X, which has been marked in the second photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you invite the witness to point at the map where that approximately is on the map. So the point from where the photograph was taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krsman, can you point out the position from which this photograph was taken on the map.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: As there aren't any houses that have been marked here, I assume that it is at the position where we can see the number "16" and "17."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And could we then know that the upper photograph, in what direction is that photograph taken from point 16/17? So what way -- in what direction are we looking from that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are looking in the direction of this photograph, which we can see in the first photograph. So from position X, we are looking in the direction of the first photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I want to know in what direction the photograph is taken, the first photograph -- so if you start at the map at 16/17 and would you then please point in the direction we are looking in when we watch this photograph. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the direction goes from this point, from the number 16/17 in the direction of this circle here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. Could we now again move to the first photograph. Could we zoom in, please. Is there any structure on this photograph - and just, I'm not asking about structures that are circled - but can you identify any structure on this photograph of which you know where it is on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the first house that you can see next to this power line, this is Veso Bozic's house and every year I went there for his name day. All these houses in the photograph belong to the Bozic family. And the ones further to the right belong to the Tomic family, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you -- the first house you mentioned, you said the Bozic's house, could you first point at it on the photograph again exactly what house you have in mind. I think you said left from the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And could you now point at the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first house from this power line here. I said "up to the power line."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please point at it, the house you have in mind exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you now point at the map where that house is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right next to the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness is now pointing at a position just left from the red circle on the map where a interrupted line ends in a red line, approximately, on the scale of the map, 100 metres left from the red circle. Could you please invite the witness to mark that on the map, Ms. Pilipovic. So Bozic's house you just mentioned, could you --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krsman, could you mark this on the map. Could you mark that house on the map.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: That house has been marked on the real map. But as I really can't tell with precision --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I'll later ask you to mark that house on the real map, since you say it has been marked.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At least that's clear now. Ms. Pilipovic, could you try to go through the map as systematically as possible, because it creates a lot of confusion, and the Chamber really wants to understand it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krsman, can you take the map D1843, since you said that the map -- the house was marked on that map. And could you mark it on that map so that everything is clear to us.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes. That's probably the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we zoom in in the relevant area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've marked the house with the letter "K" and with a little square.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Our positions were right next to that house.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you told us that this road passed through -- and on this map we can see that it more or less divided these two areas and UNPROFOR used this road. Can you tell us whether UNPROFOR was present in your brigade's zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes, it was present for a certain period of time in the Rajlovac barracks. But since they were not very secure there -- security was not very good, they had an observation post in Reljevo and UNPROFOR had an office in Upa [phoen], the distribution centre. They would come there and they would make certain suggestions. Truces were discussed, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You have mentioned the presence of UNPROFOR in the barracks. For the period from September 1992 until August 1994, can you tell us whether UNPROFOR was present in the area of your brigade's zone of responsibility. And if so, when was that?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: UNPROFOR was there all the time for another reason, because UNHCR had its warehouse -- its central warehouse in Rajlovac. It was the central warehouse for Sarajevo. And humanitarian aid would be delivered there. And then the UNHCR and UNPROFOR would provide security for that, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think I have got a precise answer for that period, September 1992/August 1994. How long was UNPROFOR present in the barracks? I haven't understood you.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Well, at the beginning of 1992 and 1993, UNPROFOR would visit the barracks. But security was not good in the barracks, and so I don't know where they were positioned. They would come and every day -- every five days they would visit the positions, the command. They would discuss matters, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: During that period, while your positions were being supervised -- well, first of all, can you tell me what sort of cooperation did you have with UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Well, our cooperation was very good even after the bombing of the NATO forces and the rapid intervention forces. Even after those events, our cooperation was quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: At any time during that period, as the company commander, did you receive any kind of protest to the effect that members of your company had been shelling civilians and civilian features?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Throughout the wartime period - and this can be found in their records for sure - we never received a protest, not a single protest. And what is more, we even delivered a protest to them about enemy action. And there is not a single document in which my company would be accused or the brigade, and that was for the entire wartime period, not just for this period you have mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that there was a distribution centre in Rajlovac and that the UNHCR was present there too and then humanitarian aid was distributed. That is how I've understood your testimony. Can you tell us how and to whom that humanitarian aid was distributed in that distribution centre.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Humanitarian aid wasn't distributed in the distribution centre, but humanitarian aid arrived there from the airport and then it would be shared out. Part of it would be part for the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina - that's what it was called at the time - and part of it would go to Sarajevo. There would be five trailers that would arrive every day. And then when 20 trailers were there, some would go to the town, some of the goods that had arrived in town would be taken away, and other goods would be taken to the inhabitants in Rajlovac, Vogosca, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether humanitarian aid -- how humanitarian aid was distributed in your area.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Well, humanitarian aid was distributed just like everything else. In local communes, there were cultural centres where humanitarian aid would be distributed on the basis of the lists, and then people would come, mostly women, and they would collect that humanitarian aid without any problems. There was never a problem of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any information about how humanitarian aid was distributed in the part of Sarajevo that was under the control of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence thinks that it's relevant since we're discussing the distribution of humanitarian aid. And since the witness himself said that humanitarian aid was distributed and he told us how this was done, I simply wanted the witness to tell us whether he knew how humanitarian aid was distributed, if he knew anything about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please. I think the -- if you think that the distribution of humanitarian aid is relevant, then the way it is done might be relevant as well. But I understand the objection of Mr. Mundis to be that the distribution of humanitarian aid, and therefore the way it was done, is not relevant for the charges brought against the accused. Is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That is, Mr. President. And of course the fact that we don't object to the first few questions doesn't necessarily mean that that entire line of questioning would somehow become relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We heard a lot of evidence on the distribution of humanitarian aid, and sometimes it was related to incidents or to going from smuggling to people lining up for receiving humanitarian aid. So there was always a clear link between, I would say, things that are in the -- that we are focussing on and that are very much in dispute. I think the question here is whether in general what is the relevance of this information. Let's first wait and see how the witness answers that question, and let's then -- perhaps you could then use the break in order to find out what the relevance would be of any further questions in this direction. So the question was how the humanitarian aid was distributed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that it was distributed in the same way that it was distributed for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please, Ms. Pilipovic, during the break consider just for yourself how important details on how humanitarian Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. aid was distributed on one side of the line and the other side of the line. We'll then hear from you and your next questions. We'll adjourn until five minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to inform the parties, the draft that was prepared -- but perhaps we should not deal with it in open session. But the document indicated yesterday is available for the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just need one further clarification, and then I will have finished with my examination. Could the witness be shown photograph 1812A.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krsman, you marked in the left-hand corner next to the column the Bozic house, and you also marked the Bozic house on the town map. And on map 1884, where incident 16 and 17 have been marked, you also marked the Bozic house. In the upper photograph, bearing in mind the map and the town map, would it be logical for you for the road to be seen, the main road, in this photograph too?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Well, it would be quite logical for one to be able to see the road and the railway line and everything else that one would have seen from this position to this position, 16 and 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us, bearing in mind that in the upper photograph you can't see the road -- in your opinion, from which position was this photograph taken, the upper photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, asked and answered, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the witness has two times answered that question. So, therefore, it's unclear to me what -- is there -- if you would like to explain, we should do that in the absence of the witness. But the question as such without further explanation is not admissible. But you're invited to give any explanation why the question should be put to the witness for the third time, if there's any reason to do so, but that should then be done in the absence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just wanted the witness to identify the road, to tell us whether the main road could be seen in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness has testified that it would be quite logical to see the main road, which I understood to say that you do not see the main road. I mean, otherwise, it's not a matter of logic but, rather, a question of pointing at it. So if you want to seek further information in that respect, you're free to do so. And again, if there's a good reason to put the question for the third time to the witness, you're invited to explain it but not in the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I just wanted to show the photograph to the witness, a photograph in which according to what the witness pointed out to on the map and -- on map 1884, where he marked the location of Bozica Kuca, Bozica houses. I wanted to show him the photograph where he marked the Bozica house. I just wanted to avoid any confusion and he confirmed that it should be possible to see the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me then try to -- Witness, may I ask you: I took it from your answer that you do not see the main road. Have you any explanation on why you do not see the main road on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think the photograph was taken in such a way that the road can't be seen, but you can see the facility which is further down below in this circle, and I think that this was done on purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whether it was done on purpose or not is a different matter. Is your explanation that the view on the road is taken by the hill and the slope which appear in the foreground? Is it because of the hill that you can't see the road, or might be just down the hill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that the difference of altitude was 200 metres. That's perhaps the reason for which you can't see the road. But I can't say anything for certain because you can't see the road and it should be possible to see it. You can't see the railway line, and it should be possible to see it too. It's up to the Chamber to decide what is at stake. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you said it was done on purpose. Could you explain what you meant by that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I have understood this correctly, attempts are being made to prove that we fired from this location to another location, at another position, that the Serbs fired from one position at another position. Naturally it should be visible. And in the first photograph, visibility is good, when you have a look at the first photograph. But as I know that area very well, I really don't know how it was photographed, where it was photographed from. So this is why I assumed that the photographer went down below to photograph it from such a position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If this photograph was taken for that purpose in your view, that is, that positions held by your forces are visible and that it is in support of allegations that your forces might have fired, would that structure in the circle, would that be in the area held by your forces? So the structure in the circle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They didn't fire from a facility inside this circle. Absolutely not. Our forces were at least 150 metres behind these houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say this is not in the territory held by your forces.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This circle isn't in the territory that was held by our forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since you expressed as your view that deliberately this photograph was taken to support that your forces might be held responsible for whatever has happened on this place, could you tell us by whose forces that area in the circle was held, if it was not yours. Or was it held by no party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That territory wasn't held by any party, because it was impossible to survive there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, if there are any further questions, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, is the Prosecution ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution has no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Nieto-Navia has one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to continue with the photograph, please. I know that we can't see the road, the main road, but where it should be, where it is supposed to be the main road in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Since this photograph was taken from a hill, I'm really not an expert, so I can't know what the slope is, what the slope of the hill is. I can't know everything. But the road, according to the map -- if this is the place, and it's more or less here, it should be in front of this position. There should be the railway line first and then the road and then it climbs up towards the hill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: In front of which position?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: You said "it should be in front of this position." I am asking which position are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: I said that this little house was in front of our position, and I don't know what this thing in the circle is. In front of the photograph there should be an open space and then there would be the railway line that goes to the city, and then after the railway line the road should be there, and then the ground slopes upwards towards the position indicated by the number "16" and "17." Why it's not there, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown map 1844, I think is the map. That one, yes. The grey line in which the red spot 16/17 is marked on that map, is that the road?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: But that road cannot be seen in the photograph either; right?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: If you're referring to this road --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: -- That descends from number 16 and 17, you can only see 4 or 5 metres of it in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I would like to see the photograph again.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: You see, you can see the road which is descending here. I don't know how long it is, but you can only see a small part of the road, if that's the road and if it was photographed from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Would you point again at the place of the road.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: See, here, this supporting wall -- this retaining wall. You can see very well how this is asphalt and how the road descends. And of course it goes up too. Now, again, once again I say that is the place from which the photograph was taken, because this photograph shows that the road also climbs up. Therefore, it also ascends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I would like to see the first photograph again. The lower part of the photograph is part of a road?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Judge El Mahdi has also one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Witness, I'd like to seek two small clarifications from you. First -- the first has to do with civilian targets. You answered a question that was asked of you, and I will quote you in English: [In English] " There were no civilians." And then further on you said, and I quote: [In English] "Considered the mosque to be a civilian target. But as there was a tank and a gun, it was a legitimate military target." [Interpretation] So my question is as follows: Did you fire at the mosque? Let me explain. I'd really like to understand exactly what you are saying. You are telling us that the mosque -- since there was a tank there and there was a gun there, near the mosque, and that therefore you did not consider the mosque as a civilian target. Am I to take this, that you considered it as a military target, as a military facility and therefore a legitimate target for an attack?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Well, you can see on the photograph number 2 this mosque, which you can see in the background, if I can point at it. This is the mosque I was referring to. It's here. Don't you see it? So it is at the highest point of Sokolje. It is at the highest point on the Sokolje. There was a tank next to that mosque, and it was quite natural for us to fire at the tank which was next to the mosque. So it was a legitimate target, regardless of where it was. In this case, it was next to the mosque, but we were not aiming at the mosque but at the tank which was next to the mosque, and it was quite a legitimate target. The Muslims wanted to represent it as if we were targeting the mosque, but we were not targeting the mosque. We were targeting the tank next to the mosque, and the same holds true of the gun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, you agree, or is it that you want to say that the mosque as such was not a military target but that you wanted to hit the tank which was near the mosque? And did then that your mortars -- that your projectiles simply miss the target and hit the mosque by mistake? Was it a tank which was stationary, which never moved, which never made any manoeuvres?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: No, it wasn't stationary. It manoeuvred. And I told you, when their attacks were, it would come then. But the -- our devices are all very precise, and we didn't often go off the mark, but sometimes it happened because of the weather conditions or something. It didn't happen often, but it did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you used, what, mortars or what kind of weapons? Do you remember a specific case when you opened the fire on the tank which was stationed and which opened fire on you and the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. tank which was very near the mosque?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: A mortar is never used against heavy weapons. The mortar is used to destroy enemy troops. So mortars are never used against tanks. We used the recoilless gun against the tank or a Howitzer if possible. But we didn't have it all the time. So as a rule we used the recoilless gun, and it is a very precise weapon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very good. Did you know, were you informed, did you know, were you aware of the provisions of the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes. Every morning during the briefings - I've already said that - we received instructions not to target civilians. But truth to tell, I am not familiar with all the provisions of the Geneva Conventions. But I am aware of the basic principles of the law of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you very much. My last question is: Was Bacici in your area, in the area that was held by your troops, or was Bacici on the opposite side?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: I drew on the map the territory that we held. We did not occupy anything, that is Serb land on which we lived. So it is our private property. All that I drew on the land is the property of Republika Srpska and is Serb land, and Serbs lived there. That is, we had lived there for more than two, three or more hundred years, it varies from family to family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I understand you. But my question is: Bacici -- Bacici, was it under your control?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Bacici was in the interspace. That is, before the war, Bacici belonged to us. But as it could not be defended efficiently, nobody could survive there, we retreated from there to those houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes. Right. But listen to me. Was Bacici in the territory -- in your territory and then you withdrew from there and left it? And that was when, more or less, that you withdrew from there, that you left this part of the territory?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Well, no, not approximately. On the 9th of May, 1992 exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1992?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes. As I have said, as immediately after the first attack against the Rajlovac barracks on the 8th of May, this population fled from there and we left it because it was simply impossible to defend. It was indefencible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. But you are talking about the time before May 1992. That is, the lines were not the same, were they?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: No. On the map I showed you that we helped -- not helped but that people lived there right up next to the Bozica pump. And that also covered the territory of Bacici. The man went to work. It was his petrol station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But was it until May, until the 8th of May, 1992? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes. And on the 8th of May, when we were attacked, it was the frontal attack against this territory, as I have said. People withdrew. It didn't matter the financial resources -- the material resources. What matters is life. And that is why we withdrew and that remained. So that was the area between us until the end of the war. It was no man's land.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've got a few questions for you as well. The first question is about refugees in the barracks. You told us about them. Were there many refugees in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: There were waves of refugees coming to the barracks, that is, whenever there would be an exodus of Serbs from different parts of Sarajevo, large numbers of people would arrive in the barracks. Therefore, Brijesce, Bujakov Potok, Pofalici. From Pofalici, 300 people arrived on -- in a single day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't ask you where they came from. I asked you whether there were many. And I think you responded that in the affirmative. Were the barracks big enough to house them all?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Did not stay. Not all of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But were the barracks big enough to house all these refugees?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes. It could accommodate 10.000 cadets before the war, which means that it could accommodate a large number of the population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And would -- do you have a guess of an estimate of how many refugees there were?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: It must have been not less than 3.000 refugees who had passed through the barracks and about 300 of them stayed on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Were they in specific parts of the barracks, or were they all over the barracks?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: In the beginning of the war, the refugees were all over. Simply because people were inexperienced. But as they began to die, we transferred them to other buildings were not directly exposed to the front line. But in the early days they were all over, and I think we paid that dearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness be shown again the Exhibit 1843, the map. Could you tell us where the refugees were concentrated. What part of the barracks?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: See here, this is the main road which goes through the barracks. You can see it is drawn here. Behind it were the refugees. And in front of this main road was the canteen, where the refugees had their meals and the troops later on, so in front of the road. All these are dormitories because this was the training centre. And they were in these buildings here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was the same canteen used for the soldiers and the refugees, or had you -- did you have more canteens?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: It was the same canteen. And for the duration of the war, we all had our meals there. But I said that when the war started, the real war, later on, after the army was formed, nobody could be considered a refugee. So they were all either soldiers or people doing something with the army. So until June 1992, we were no longer refugees. We were an army then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said, as far as I remember, the children were not there any more after a certain moment. And women? Or did I -- I'm not quite sure that I -- women would stay in the barracks? Is that a correct understanding of your testimony, while children were transferred to another place?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Naturally, elderly women left. Women with small children left. But there were women who worked in the kitchen, in the laundry, and so on and so forth. They stayed on. There were also military conscripts. And it only so happened that they found refuge there. But otherwise, they were military conscripts just like the rest of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You'd say the women remaining in the barracks were all militarily active, either in the kitchen or whatever way, but in order to support the military.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then some last few questions for you. Could perhaps the photograph be put on the ELMO again. On the upper photograph, the structure in a circle, in a black circle, do you recognise what it is?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you be able to point at the map or the maps, D1844 - let's start with D1844 - the exact location of that building after you've told us what it is.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: I've already said. It's a structure in the field. Perhaps it was a tool shed. Perhaps it was a hen coop or something. I don't know what it is. I mean, it is not habitable, not for humans, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please on the map indicate where it is.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: This structure is somewhere in this red circle, perhaps -- perhaps a bit forward. But roughly there somewhere. Because this map is not a good map. That is, the scale has not been transferred accurately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the other map better? Could you indicate on the other map where that building is?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Well, it is roughly -- roughly, it is here, where these two lines meet. Roughly here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you now take the photograph again. You're now looking down the hill, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does the structure appear to the right or to the left of the house you indicated on the map by "K"?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Which house?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The house in the circle -- or the structure in the circle, I should say. The house you said that you -- on the map you indicated that a house -- you put a "K" on it. I've forgotten exactly what the name is. Wasn't it Bozic's house, the house just left from the electricity pole on this picture. You indicated that it would be at a position you marked with "K" on the map. Is the structure in the circle to the right or to the left of that house?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: This is to the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you look at the photograph, at Bozic's house, could you please point at it again.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Bozica houses are all behind this structure, which is in the circle. So this is all behind it. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Didn't you point at a house to the left of the pole when you previously indicated where Bozic's house was?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Well, I've already told you that I couldn't see any houses to the left, if I know what is left. There are no houses to the left of the electric pole, from the electric pole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You pointed -- could you please point again at what you pointed at before as left from the electric pole would be Bozic's house. Could you point at it again.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: No, I was talking about this as the electric pole. So to the right of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think you said left from the pole, and I think you meant to say left from the -- what appears to be a wooden pole and not a metal pole. Could you point at it again, the -- could you first point at the pole, to make sure that we have the same pole in mind.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is -- seems to be a metal -- metallic electrical pole.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you now point at the pole you pointed at earlier, which is the pole closest to the position where the photograph was taken and which has the appearance of a wooden pole rather than an electric pole, in the foreground. Could you point at that.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: This pole here, which is right next -- below the road, a metre or two. And that is why I said that the photograph was taken from this angle on purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's what you told us. Could you then, please, again point at Bozic's house, as you did before. You said that it was to the left of that pole, the last pole you indicated. Could you please point at it again, Bozic's house.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Here it is and all these houses here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When you earlier pointed at Bozic's house, did you point at all the houses or just the house left to the wooden pole?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: I said that all these houses belonged to the Bozic family, and this one is the one that I visited and I know which of the Bozics it belongs to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's the one you marked on the map?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Well, it's not shown on the map, but I can say approximately. Of course, I can be mistaken because there are no houses indicated on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You marked the place where that house was on the map; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, could you again tell me whether from this angle of view the structure in the circle is to the right or to the left of Bozic's house, that part of Bozic's house of which you know who lives in it or lived in it. Is it to the right or is it to the left?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Well, judging by this photograph, then this building is to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: On this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you said -- could perhaps the witness be shown 1844 again. You said that the structure that was in a circle would have to have been situated in the red circle on this map. Do you remember that you told us this?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I said more or less. If -- I mean, this circle is very big, so it could be in the centre of the circle or it could be at its left -- on the left-hand side. So I said that roughly this is the house and roughly this is somewhere here. But it's somewhere there, more or less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would look from -- if you would take the position at 16/17. If you would look at Bozic's house as you indicated it on the map, the small rectangle. Is the circle from that point of view to the left or to the right of Bozic's house?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: If we look at the map, it's to the right. But in the photograph, as I said, the photograph had been taken on purpose from that position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I asked to tell me -- I asked you to tell me whether it would be on the left or on the right viewed from position indicated by 16/17. So you'd have to turn the map.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: I can see it in the map. As I said, as I described it, to the right of Bozic's house. But in the photograph, it's to the left. And I said why it was as it was in the photograph, and if necessary I can explain this to you if you put the photograph back on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so. Explain to us.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: If the photograph had really been taken from position X, then the containers down below would be visible. They can't be seen in the first photograph. If it had been photographed from X, these containers here would have been visible. So he took up a position to the left on purpose so that the photograph would represent what it represented. I can't see what other explanation could be provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: I don't know what the purpose was, but the photograph wasn't taken from position X.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it taken from that same road near to where the containers are, but, say, within a distance of 10, 15, 20 metres?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Well, perhaps even more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it taken from the same road as the road that is shown on the lower photograph?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: As I've already said, first of all you can't see the railway line and then you can't see the main road, so -- I know this area, but I didn't take this photograph, so I can't claim that it was taken from the same road. Perhaps it was; perhaps it wasn't. The person who took the photograph must know this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I'm just asking you whether you're suggesting that it was not taken from that road or that you don't know. You know the area. That's the reason why I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: I think the photograph was taken from the same road but not from the position that has been marked with "X."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Lower down or higher up?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Lower down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: A lot lower than position X.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A lot? How much? You say a lot. How much?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: I'm not an expert, but 50 metres lower down for sure because the road descends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for your answers. Judge Nieto-Navia has another question for you as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. You recall that you mentioned how the humanitarian aid was distributed.

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Well, I have a question: The places where humanitarian aid was distributed, did they change from time to time or were always the same places?

utterances.speaker: SINISA KRSMAN
utterances.text: There was no reason to make any changes. Throughout the wartime period, the places at which humanitarian aid was distributed never changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there are no further questions from the parties. I'd like to thank you, Mr. Krsman, for coming to The Hague. We know that it takes some time and it's a great distance. And I'd like to thank you that you've answered all the questions that have been put to you. And I wish that you'll have a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you please guide us through the documents tendered in respect of this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1843, map marked by witness; Exhibit D1844, map, sniping incident 16 and 17 marked by witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, it's almost time. I don't expect the witness still to be there for the last ten minutes, although it's contrary to my -- the habit of this Chamber to use the time fully. Your next witness would be -- on the list I see that it would be Professor Cavoski.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Professor Kosta Cavoski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it's not wise to start with him for the last ten minutes. No formal decision has yet been given on the time, but perhaps we should do that at least in respect of the first witness. You just asked for more time, Mr. Mundis, or at least Mr. Ierace did so, one hour and a half. But it was compensated by less time for another expert witness. It is a background witness. The balance between the time used by the party that called the witness and that cross-examined the witness, especially for the background witnesses, was far in favour of the cross-examining party when the Prosecution's case was presented. The Chamber allows one hour and a half for cross-examination. And Ms. Pilipovic, I see that I think you claimed also one hour Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and a half for Professor Cavoski. Is that right? Because I think the Chamber granted until now - although no formal decision has been taken on your request to reconsider - but that was not in respect to this witness, as far as I remember. Or was it? You asked for four hours, I think, or six hours? Six hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, your decision has to do with the expert who will be discussing the background. These are Professors Kosta Cavoski, Mrs. Jelena Guskova, and Mr. Slavenko Terzic. You allowed three hours in your decision. And the decision was to use these three hours for those three experts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have on my list -- but that's just a schedule. I don't -- I take it that it's prepared on the basis of your meetings that you would need one hour and a half for Professor Cavoski, one hour and a half for expert witness Guskova, and ten minutes for expert witness Terzic -- is that? Three hours and ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
